`rglob("*")` is broader than what weaver reads:

- It picks up `.git/`, `.venv/`, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/` and editor swap files. With `--registry .`, every run reads the whole git object store into memory, even when the cache is hit. Any `git fetch` or saved `.swp` file also changes the digest, so the model is rebuilt.
- On Python versions before 3.13 (we support >=3.10), `rglob` doesn't descend into symlinked folders but weaver does. Edits under a symlinked `model/shared -> ../../common/model` won't change the digest.

Hashing only `*.yaml` / `*.yml` / `*.json` (and following symlinks) would fix both, and is cheaper too.

Override models now land in the shared `coverage-models/` folder instead of a temporary folder per session. That brings two problems:

- `resolve()` does an unlocked `output.is_file()` check, then fills `output` with `shutil.move` from `/tmp`. That is a copy between filesystems, so it isn't atomic. Two parallel runs over the same `--registry` (CI jobs, xdist workers) can catch the file half-written, and `load()` then fails with a `JSONDecodeError`. Moving to a temp name in `output.parent` and then calling `os.replace(tmp, output)` would fix it.
- Nothing prunes this folder. Each edit to a working-tree registry leaves another full model behind, so a persisted CI cache or a local dev loop grows without limit. Keeping only the latest model per registry name might be enough.

Weaver also reads `.weaver.toml`, looking for it from the working directory upwards. Its `[registry]` section can set `include_unreferenced` and `follow_symlinks`, and both change what gets resolved. Neither this digest nor `fingerprint()` covers that file. Editing it, or running from a directory that finds a different one, reuses a model resolved with the old settings. Pinned models have the same gap.

It's rare in practice: semantic-conventions' own `.weaver.toml` only has policy filters. Two possible fixes: hash the `.weaver.toml` that weaver would find into `fingerprint()`, which covers both kinds of model. Or pass weaver's global `--config` with a fixed file, which skips discovery, so the working directory no longer matters.
